story: On Wednesday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is on Magnolia Loop with a determined look, promising Hal he'll redo his street-side sketch tonight and bring it by tomorrow. Hal, content as ever, has agreed to show up Friday evening on time and bring whatever Rosa asks for. Rosa, warm and hopeful, is counting on Gary's cornbread and Hal's attendance, and she just needs to coax Donna, who is upbeat and heading out onto the street, to join them at the table.
events: Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Hal said the sketch needs to show the lights and speaker mounts from the street side with every measurement marked. That's the fix before filing. Rosa already got her yes on Friday, and I offered cornbread, so no need to ask again. Best move now is to tell Hal I'm heading home to redo the sketch, then get it done. Keep it short, thank him, and go do the work.

parameters.content: Understood, Hal. Street-side view, every measurement marked. I'll redo the sketch tonight and bring it by tomorrow. Thanks for the sharp eye.

donna.thought_process: I've already checked the calendar, the phone, and the pickleball bag over the last few ticks. Gary hasn't answered yet, and nagging him again would just be pushy. Nobody's nearby, and it's Wednesday afternoon with Tuesday's court slot already penciled in. The sensible thing is to stop fussing and get on with my day, which means a short walk down Magnolia Loop to catch up with neighbors. That's how I stay at the center of things and hear who's saying what about the ladder before next week.

parameters.content: Heading out for a stroll down Magnolia Loop to see which neighbors are out and catch up on the ladder gossip while Gary gets back to me.

hal.thought_process: Gary and Rosa are both here on Magnolia Loop. Rosa's pinned note invited all three of us, and I already told Gary I'd be there, but I haven't answered Rosa directly. Telling her plainly settles it, and I can offer to bring something in my own gruff way. I already gave Gary his corrections last tick, so no need to repeat them. Then I can get back to my watchdog duties.

parameters.content: Saw your note, Rosa. Friday evening, I'll be there on time, because I'm always on time. Tell me what to bring and I'll bring it.

rosa.thought_process: Gary said yes and offered cornbread, Hal said he'll be there. That's two of three. Donna is the missing one, and her flamingos are right here, so she's probably around her house. I already invited everyone on the bulletin board and shouldn't repeat myself. Gary offered cornbread and hasn't heard my answer yet. A quick yes to the cornbread is useful, and it keeps the dinner moving. Then I'll go find Donna in person.

parameters.content: Cornbread would be perfect, Gary, bring it. Hal says he's in too, so now I just need to get Donna to the table.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
